extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and current comedy bookers, producers, talent managers, and readers interested in the L.A. stand-up scene
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for programming, producing, and booking stand-up comedy shows in Los Angeles, covering talent selection, venue management, audience fit, safety, and community development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye for talent / ability to identify talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Bookers must be able to identify, source and schedule talent — having 'an eye for talent' is a prerequisite for the role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes scouting, negotiating deals with agents, and selecting comics who will resonate on a stage; 'if you have found yourself in the position of being a booker regardless of your sex, you’ve proven yourself to have an eye for talent.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and maintain vibe/tone onstage
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers should set the tone for shows — 'vibe creation' and 'creating the work that sets the tone onstage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involves inspiration, decision-making, question-asking, content creation, posting and curating lineups so the evening feels cohesive and intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize performer and audience safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs and bookers must uphold standards that keep the workplace and venue safe for all performers and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-#MeToo safety practices, refusing sexual assaulters, and setting rules/policies to protect performers and patrons; building a safe environment was cited as a reason to open new spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion in programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively diversify talent rosters to include voices historically absent from mainstream media (LGBTQIA+, people of color, disabled performers, women, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bookers reported making concerted efforts to diversify lineups and seeking voices 'that have not been present in mainstream media'; lack of diversity often reflects the picker, not the pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize stage-suitability over social metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't rely solely on follower counts, engagement or algorithm-driven metrics when evaluating a comedian's fit for live shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social media exposure can distort hiring choices — many algorithmic or viral performers may not translate to the live stage; bookers must weigh craft over pure online popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate and develop comedy community and careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Bookers are responsible for curating, cultivating and developing comics — watching, developing and challenging performers toward paid regular status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes scouting, mentoring, giving stage time, creating pathways to become paid regulars, and building a supportive local community rather than gatekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match programming to venue mission and audience appetite
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming should align with the venue's mission statement and the expectations of its audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find or create shows that match the club’s goals (e.g., safe spaces, unique voices); a progressive audience may expect programming that is 'weird and truer' or curated in a particular way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional logistics and clear communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective booking includes scheduling, negotiating, backend administration, communication, and troubleshooting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Day-to-day duties include responding to emails, coordinating with venue staff (A/V, photographers), marketing, corporate booking, and overall organizational management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek high-quality material and sophisticated comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Bookers reported audiences now crave and expect a 'higher grade of content/jokes/material.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming choices should favor well-crafted, thoughtful material rather than low-effort or purely offensive content; audiences are more educated and worldly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse to book harmful or abusive performers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not book people who make others feel bad or otherwise harm the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical booking means avoiding 's— people' and those who belittle or bully; prioritize the well-being of performers and staff when making lineup decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure venue accessibility and physical inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Make venue spaces accessible for all body types and mobilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider physical accessibility and comfort when selecting and setting up venues so performers and audiences of varied needs can participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide safe testing grounds for new material
rubrics_metrics.description: Create shows specifically designed as safe spaces for professionals to test new material (e.g., Crack’Em Up Thursdays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming that allows comics to 'work out' material in a supportive environment helps craft development and protects performers from harmful exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt booking approaches to changing platforms and landscapes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the internet, streaming, podcasts and social platforms have altered how comics build audiences and gain visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bookers should factor multi-platform exposure into decisions but not be controlled by platform metrics; be flexible as the media landscape evolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create opportunities for underrepresented performers (stage time equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively provide stage time and opportunities to performers who face historical inequities (women, people of color, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some venues were opened specifically to provide more stage time for those who haven't had equal access; booking choices can directly address systemic imbalances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice sensitivity, patience, and low-ego leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: A booking style that emphasizes sensitivity, patience and less ego fosters better relations with comics and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasted with past 'yell and bully' industry behaviors, contemporary bookers often prioritize collaborative problem-solving and emotional intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain fairness in pay and opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of and work to correct pay and opportunity discrepancies across gender and racial lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women bookers noted greater awareness of pay gaps; ethical programming includes equitable compensation and transparent opportunity structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curate lineups that align with audience expectations and tastes
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the audience's appetite and the club's brand when assembling a lineup to ensure resonance and longevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A progressive or 'hip' audience may prefer contemporary, truthful voices; mismatch between programming and audience can affect show success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance boundary-pushing with awareness of cancel culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Bookers and performers must navigate pushing comedic boundaries while being mindful of cultural backlash and self-censorship pressures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some creators feel constrained by 'cancel culture' and weigh how far to push material versus potential reputational or community consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop producers and shows that fit club mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek hardworking producers whose shows align with the club’s mission and quality expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bookers may curate producers and external shows to broaden programming, but selections should match the venue’s goals and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in marketing and promotion to build audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective marketing, advertising and promotion are part of successful programming and booking duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond talent selection, clubs must actively promote shows, build audience relationships, and use outreach to ensure shows fill nights and performers gain exposure.
